sources.title: Ask-Elle: an Adaptable Programming Tutor for Haskell Giving Automated Feedback
sources.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education 27:65–100
sources.design: Three technical/user evaluations; model-solution recognition and property-based feedback; no controlled learning comparison.
sources.population: University Haskell learners; different course cohorts.
sources.findings: Stepwise hints can address partial programs and counterexamples. The 2013 evaluation contains 1,920 compiler-error interactions (55.4% of diagnoses), but 142 of 652 attempts (21.8%) ended in compiler error. These are interaction/attempt denominators, not learner prevalence. Authors explicitly leave learning effects to future work.
sources.limitations: Accuracy, coverage and perceived usefulness do not establish retention or transfer. Recognition depends on model solutions and supported strategies; alternative valid programs may be unrecognized.

sources.title: Teaching Introductory Functional Programming Using Haskelite
sources.design: Teaching experience, voluntary qualitative feedback and historical course results.
sources.population: Porto first-year students, mostly prior Python; spring 2024.
sources.findings: Learners reported usefulness for inspecting recursion and higher-order functions. Trace size and unsupported valid Haskell syntax created difficulties; the tool needs explicit subset messages. Distinguish the tool's six-response questionnaire from the separate institutional fifteen-response course survey.
sources.limitations: Small self-selected feedback; course changes and historical pass rates cannot identify the tool's causal effect. Tool implements a Haskell subset. Short semantic traces are not an exact account of optimized GHC execution.

sources.title: Evaluating Haskell expressions in a tutoring environment
sources.design: Prototype and small formative usability survey.
sources.findings: The prototype diagnoses learner-entered rewrite steps under different evaluation strategies. Respondents differed over how much strategy choice and detail learners should see.
sources.limitations: Feasibility and usability evidence; no controlled learning gains. Small response groups. Multiple strategies may overwhelm beginners, so a default strategy is an instructional choice to test.
provenance: Consensus teaching discovery; primary independently verified

sources.title: Experiences of early assessment to teach functional programming
sources.design: Historical-cohort comparison, online first-year course during COVID, 2021 versus 2022.
sources.population: First-year discrete-mathematics/Haskell course; students completing both assessments.
sources.findings: Adding an early summative Use-Modify assessment accompanied a later Create-assessment mean of 62.249 versus 53.256: 8.993 percentage points; one-tailed Wilcoxon p=.0371, reported r=.164. Both cohorts already used formative Use-Modify-Create.
sources.limitations: Small reported effect, nonrandom cohorts, completer selection, changed recordings and other context; mathematics means decreased. Association cannot establish causality or delayed transfer.
provenance: Direct OpenAlex forward citations from Tirronen2015

sources.title: Learner experiences of a blended course incorporating a MOOC on Haskell functional programming
sources.design: Survey and focus group in blended honours course; no randomized comparator.
sources.population: Fourth-year Glasgow students, 2016–17; first six of ten weeks used a MOOC.
sources.findings: Respondents valued flexibility and learning activities but reported poorly signposted support and discontinuity into more advanced work. Integration of help and progression warrants design attention.
sources.limitations: Self-selected perceptions, not demonstrated learning effects. One advanced university course; cannot rank MOOCs against classroom teaching.

sources.title: Using Student-created Instructional Videos in CS Upper-level Courses: A Successful Strategy in a Functional Programming Course
sources.design: Small uncontrolled pre/post classroom experience with two student-made explanatory videos.
sources.population: Senior functional-programming course at Universidad El Bosque, Colombia; ages 18–35.
sources.findings: Assessment improvement and positive perceptions accompanied students making concept/code explanation videos; participants also found production time-consuming.
sources.limitations: No comparator; improvement can reflect normal course learning, practice or selection. Do not equate video production with a demonstrated causal self-explanation effect or transfer to beginner Haskell.

sources.title: The risks and benefits of teaching purely functional programming in first year
sources.design: Teaching experience based on several large first-year classes and surveys; detail not independently extracted.
sources.findings: Abstract frames functional programming as a means to teach problem solving and computer science rather than paradigm advocacy as an end.
sources.limitations: Full text not inspected; no causal claim about benefits or harm, and no extracted effect size.
